locator.section: web/www/missa/Latin/Ordo/Prayers.txt [Per eumdem], section line 107; full conclusion and R. Amen. at lines 108–109

entries.claim: The literal $Per eumdem directive in Nat2-0.txt resolves to this full conclusion and Amen response. The equal-text Per eundem alias at lines 111–113 is not the invoked section.

locator.section: web/www/missa/Latin/Tempora/Nat2-0.txt [Oratio], section line 20; body line 21 and $Per eumdem reference line 22

entries.claim: The pinned Latin Mass file supplies the Collect body and its literal $Per eumdem reference. The conclusion is separately resolved from the declared Prayers.txt dependency; this file alone is not a continuous full-text witness.

locator.section: Sanctissimi Nominis Iesu, Oratio; body and abbreviated Per eundem Dominum cue

entries.claim: The approved Benziger printing gives the 28-word Collect body followed by the abbreviated Per eundem Dominum cue. It does not print the complete expanded conclusion on this page.

locator.section: Postcommunio continuing Monday after the first Sunday of the Passion, above the Tuesday heading; Dominum nostrum through Deus.

entries.claim: This separate Postcommunion prints the accented middle conclusion, including no comma after Christum and the colon and uppercase Qui after tuum, ending with Deus. The composite uses Dominum nostrum through Deus.; this page supplies neither eundem nor the final duration or Amen.

locator.section: Top conclusion and response before the Nativity preface dialogue; Per omnia saecula saeculorum. R. Amen.

entries.claim: The top chant line prints Per omnia saecula saeculorum and the response Amen. The composite joins musical syllable divisions and omits the response marker. Only these five words are used; the Nativity preface dialogue and body are excluded, and this location does not establish Collect delivery.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 a; Father-addressed oration conclusion and response

entries.claim: RG 115 a supplies the full Father-addressed conclusion and the separate Amen response. It controls the expansion rule, not the selected composite transcript's accents or its accidental seams.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 b; mention of the Son at the beginning of an oration

entries.claim: RG 115 b prescribes Per eundem Dominum nostrum, etc., ut supra when an oration addressed to the Father mentions the Son at its beginning. The Holy Name body and printed cue instantiate this rule; the different end-mention rule in 115 c is not used here.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 511 d; orations in a read Mass

entries.claim: RG 511 d includes the orations among the parts said aloud by the celebrant in a read Mass. This supports the Collect's clara delivery; it is not the Secret's final audible-ending rule.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 513 a and 514; orations in solemn and sung Mass

entries.claim: RG 513 a includes the orations among the celebrant's sung parts in solemn Mass, and RG 514 extends the singing rule to sung Mass. These rules support the Collect's cantus delivery, not exclusive assignment of Amen to a choir.
